extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing a Memoir (monograph) for submission to the American Mathematical Society (AMS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing AMS Memoirs-class LaTeX manuscripts, covering citations, floats, graphics, bibliographies, indexing, permissions, file submission, and production-ready technical requirements. Intended to ensure production-quality source files for AMS publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard citation commands
rubrics_metrics.description: The style of reference citations is usually roman; always use the standard LaTeX \cite command when citing a reference (natbib provides alternate forms for author-year style).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal references with \ref are not automatically roman in non-roman environments—use the upref package to force roman. Use \eqref for references to numbered equations (it includes parentheses and roman type).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise environment usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the xca environment for producing exercises that appear individually within a section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define xca in the preamble with \theoremstyle{definition} and \newtheorem; it is used similarly to other theorem-class environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include index terms in source and run MakeIndex
rubrics_metrics.description: Index terms should be included directly in the TeX source to ensure correct page references; output must conform to MakeIndex rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run MakeIndex separately from LaTeX, then rerun LaTeX to incorporate the index. Tags for \makeindex are included in AMS classes; do not include the makeidx package. Put \makeindex in the preamble and \printindex where you want the index to appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple indexes: use amsmidx or imakeidx (not glossary)
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one index is desired, use amsmidx (AMS-written, compatible) or imakeidx; do not use a glossary package for additional indexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For amsmidx: \usepackage{amsmidx}, \makeindex{<name>}, \index{<name>}{<term>}, \Printindex{<name>}{<title>}. For imakeidx: \usepackage[original]{imakeidx}, \makeindex, \makeindex[<name>], and \printindex[name=<name>,title=<title>]. The [original] option preserves AMS formatting for the first index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Float numbering and placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Floats (figures and tables) should be numbered consistently (figures and tables numbered separately), placed at the top or bottom of the page, have an in-text reference, and appear within the same section as their first text reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A figure or table should not precede its first text reference unless they both appear on the same page spread. When integral to text, an unnumbered in-place object may be appropriate. Allow floats to float according to class defaults and avoid hard-setting with the [h!] option to prevent production pagination problems; AMS production will determine final placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption and label placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions are usually positioned above tables and below figures; a reference label should usually be associated with the caption and must be given after the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the figure/table environment structure shown (\caption{...} then \label{...}). The caption text may be omitted if no descriptive text is desired. Caption style differs from basic LaTeX caption style; caption packages may appear to work but usually won't match AMS style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not manually center floats (AMS classes auto-center)
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS classes center the content of table and figure environments automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use \centering or \begin{center} ... \end{center} inside figure/table environments—it's unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported bibliography methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographies may be prepared using either amsrefs or BibTEX; methods using other packages (including biblatex) are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: amsrefs integrates with AMS production and MathSciNet enhancements; BibTEX styles (amsplain, amsalpha) are provided and recommended for certain uses. Enhanced references from MathSciNet can add DOIs and links; report any incorrect MR numbers to eprod-support@ams.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: BibTEX styles and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Two BibTEX styles are provided: amsplain.bst (numeric labels; preferred for articles) and amsalpha.bst (labels constructed from author name(s) and year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include \bibliographystyle{<style>} and \bibliography{<bibfile>} in the input. After running BibTEX to produce a .bbl, insert the contents of the .bbl into your input file replacing the \bibliographystyle and \bibliography statements. Items are usually ordered alphabetically by author; BibTEX may alter order (e.g., amsalpha). A language field is provided in AMS styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use natbib
rubrics_metrics.description: The natbib package provides an author-year style compatible with AMS classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily use natbib only for articles on historical topics (author-year citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Using amsrefs package
rubrics_metrics.description: amsrefs is a LaTeX package for preparing structured bibliographies that preserves structured markup throughout a document's lifetime and is compatible with showkeys, hyperref, and backrefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: amsrefs can be used by entering items directly with the biblist environment, importing from .ltb files, or importing from .bib via BibTEX with amsrefs' special styles. When using amsrefs with hyperref, load amsrefs after hyperref. Do not include a \bibliographystyle command when using amsrefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual bibliography (thebibliography) formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: If not using a bibliography package, use the thebibliography environment; choose the model label (widest label) to set proper indentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin items with \bibitem{<label>}. The printed label is the optional key in square brackets; the internal label in braces is used for linking and must not include math or special characters. Give at least one full name; use \bysame for repeated authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain permissions for third-party material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must obtain permission for any material (graphics, photographs, text) in their Work that comes from any other source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Society’s Permission Form; permissions must cover print and electronic rights for all editions (present and future), be free of restrictions limiting AMS's ability to produce/distribute the Work in any territory, language, or medium. Restricted permissions may lead to omission. Send written permission with the final manuscript and contact Acquisitions Department for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a standard graphics inclusion package (graphicx)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a standard TeX graphics inclusion macro package; the recommended package for LaTeX2e is graphicx. Ensure inclusion commands are compatible with dvips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not place graphics in subdirectories. Number figures consistently, use an in-text reference, set figure captions in TeX (below figures), make sure figures are sized correctly and do not extend into margins, and ensure overlaid labels do not extend beyond the allotted figure space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred graphics file format: EPS
rubrics_metrics.description: The preferred file format for graphics is EPS (Encapsulated PostScript); other formats will be converted to EPS at the AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics of EPS files can be checked by automated procedures, but individual features (e.g., thickness of a rule) may not be independently evaluated in a PDF graphic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bitmap graphics resolution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution requirements: line art 600 PPI at 100%; halftone 300 PPI at 100%; combination halftone 600 PPI at 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure bitmaps meet these minimums at the final printed size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create graphics at 100% printed size
rubrics_metrics.description: Create graphics at 100% of the size at which they will be printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a figure is too large, resize it in a graphics program, not in TeX. This also applies to photographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic file naming constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: File names should be no longer than 20 alphanumeric characters and should not use accented alphabetic characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly generic file names such as fig01.eps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum line/rule weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use a line/rule weight less than half a point (.5 point) at 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If scaling figures, compensate by making line weights thicker (e.g., a .5 pt line scaled to 50% becomes .25 pt and may disappear). Increase graded lines in half-point increments; screened or colored lines should be at least 1 point at 100% to avoid broken/jagged appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screens (shades of gray) limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Screens used to simulate shades of gray should not be lower than 10% or higher than 85%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen density should increase in increments of at least 10% (smaller variations are indistinguishable). Do not put (black or colored) type on a screen darker than 35% (type not legible). White type may be used only on 100% black.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fonts in graphics must be embedded and match text
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible, fonts used in graphics should match those used in text and should be fully embedded in the graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fonts cannot be embedded, convert them to paths (outlines) prior to exporting to EPS. Use Type 1 outline fonts instead of bitmap fonts. Do not subset fonts in graphics—include the full font set. Avoid using fonts named after cities (e.g., Chicago, Monaco).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-part figures: prepare as single composite
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple-part figures should be configured as one figure in a graphics program, not assembled in TeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligning multiple-part figures is difficult in TeX; composing them in a graphics program is easier and more cost-effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crop correctly and ensure correct bounding boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not crop by pasting white over parts of the graphic; instead clip or crop within the graphics application to delete unwanted areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pasting white can make the bounding box larger than it should be and cause inclusion problems. Verify bounding box information is correct to avoid clipping or misplacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color graphics: submission and print considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Color graphics submitted will appear in color online; the print version will normally appear in black and white unless special arrangements are made. Graphics intended for print in color should be submitted in CMYK format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RGB files will be converted to CMYK and conversion may not match the RGB display. Authors may pay for four-color printing for items deemed essential. For graphics to be printed in black and white/grayscale, convert to grayscale before submission and check legibility on a black-and-white printer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color gamut and conversion awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that RGB has a larger gamut than CMYK; colors outside CMYK's gamut will be approximated and may appear muted in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colors viewed on monitor or personal printer may not match press output. AMS Graphics group optimizes graphics for printed publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shades and colored line recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Inherently light colors (e.g., yellow, cyan) should be handled carefully; 50% yellow or cyan may be almost invisible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colored lines should be no less than .5 point in width; colored lines in light colors should be at or near 100% tint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type in graphics: size and contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic type size in graphics should be no less than 10 point at 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although 10 pt is acceptable for print, it may be hard to read online (72 PPI). Do not put type on a dark background; check color figures on a black-and-white printer to ensure legibility in grayscale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: width, rotation, and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure table width does not exceed the width of the text block; set table captions above the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very wide tables can be rotated using the rotating package with the sidewaystable environment. Rotate so the left-hand side of the table after rotation is at the bottom of the page. See MG chapter 5 and [voss-tbl] for more formatting help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph resolution and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs must be at a minimum resolution of 300 dpi at the actual size they will be printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not scale photographs in TeX. File formats acceptable: EPS, TIFF, or JPEG. Color photographs must be saved in CMYK format.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX-native graphics package guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Several TeX-based graphics systems are acceptable: tikz (PGF), pstricks, and xy/xypic, each with strengths and platform considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tikz/PGF works across dvips and pdfLaTeX and newer engines (XeLaTeX, LuaLaTeX); pstricks is easiest with dvips (can be used with pdfLaTeX with care); xy/xypic is useful for commutative diagrams. Consult referenced documentation and primers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling packages: check for overflow and adjust spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages that place labels on graphics ensure consistent fonts but do not modify the dimensions of a graphic; labels applied outside the graphic can extend into margins or overprint material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should carefully check graphics where external labeling was used. If labels cannot be positioned within the graphic boundaries, add extra space (e.g., with \vspace) to compensate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit exact accepted source files and include only needed files
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance, send the source file(s) used to generate the accepted copy (TeX source and graphics). Send only files needed to process or archive the submission (not .log or .aux).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify items in the basic checklist and the Memoirs class checklist. If multiple files, bundle them in a Zip to reduce name conflicts and corruption. Recommended submission via AMS web server (requires AMS account); email submissions to pub-submit@ams.org with correct subject line using the publication code; alternative FTP or physical media by arrangement. Submissions are acknowledged; problems will be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AMS resources and technical support
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult the AMS Author FAQ and AMS Technical Support for questions about preparing or submitting manuscripts electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Publications Technical Group (phone/email) or other AMS departments listed; report web server access problems to webmaster@ams.org. Use AMS TeX web pages for package downloads and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult community TeX resources
rubrics_metrics.description: For community assistance, use comp.text.tex (CTT) and tex.stackexchange.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CTT is a discussion group; tex.stackexchange is a Q&A site where participation earns privileges—read tex.stackexchange.com/about first.
